extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications industry stakeholders, FCC-regulated entities, communications lawyers, policy analysts, and members of the public tracking FCC rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: An API/listing page aggregating Federal Communications Commission final rules published in the Federal Register, including abstracts and key requirements or procedural notes for each adopted rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pole attachment rules effective date (PRA review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's revised pole attachment rules will not become effective until OMB completes its review of any information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act; the Wireline Competition Bureau will announce the effective date by subsequent Public Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: OMB approval of associated information collection is a precondition to rule effectiveness; agencies and stakeholders should monitor Bureau Public Notices for the announced effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: FM allotment minimum distance separation compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An FM channel allotment (e.g., alternate Channel 265C3 at Enterprise, Utah) must be consistent with the Commission's minimum distance separation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical criterion: allotments must satisfy FCC minimum-distance separation rules; may include site restrictions (example: 15 km west of the community) and reference coordinates. The window for filing applications may be deferred until the Commission addresses opening the allotment in a subsequent order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site restriction and reference coordinates for allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an FM/TV channel is allotted, the Commission may impose a site restriction (e.g., 15 kilometers west of the community) and provide reference coordinates (e.g., 37-35-27 NL and 113-54-02 WL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allotments with site restrictions are acceptable if they meet technical and community-coverage requirements; applicants must propose facilities consistent with the site restriction and coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service discontinuance preemption of conflicting state/local rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If state or local requirements conflict with the federal service discontinuance framework adopted by the Commission, such requirements negate valid federal regulatory objectives and are subject to preemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy principle: federal service-discontinuance framework prevails where conflict exists; state/local rules that obstruct transition to IP-based infrastructure may be preempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of facially obsolete rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will rescind facially obsolete provisions of its wireline rules to modernize its regulatory framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory objective: identify and repeal duplicative, outdated, or unnecessary rule parts to streamline and reduce regulatory burdens; some deletions may be withdrawn if significant adverse comments are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign adversary control attestations and disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range of holders of Commission-granted licenses, authorizations, or approvals must attest whether they are owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary, and if so, disclose additional information about such foreign adversary control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rules: Commission defines categories of licenses/authorizations subject to the requirement and establishes a streamlined filing process for attestations and disclosures; affected holders must follow the attestation/disclosure procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of OMB Guidance for nonprocurement debarment and suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts the Office of Management and Budget's Guidance for Nonprocurement Debarment and Suspension along with agency-specific regulations to combat waste, fraud, and abuse and remove bad actors from participation in support programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note: Commission determined further notice and comment unnecessary for adopting the Guidelines (including post-NPRM updates), but provided opportunity for input on three Guidelines; a Proposed Rule may be published for related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign ownership rules: controlling U.S. parent and remedial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules codify which entity is the controlling U.S. parent for common carrier licensees, codify advance approval policy for certain deemed voting interests, require identification of trusts and trustees, extend remedial procedures to privately held companies, add requirements for remedial petitions, require filing amendments as complete restatements, and clarify U.S. residency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application/processing guidance: Media Bureau will issue processing guidelines detailing how applications are processed during the pendency of remedial petitions; applicants and petitioners must follow new content/format requirements for remedial petitions and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 900 MHz band licensing options
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 896-901/935-940 MHz band, the Report and Order creates three options for 900 MHz licenses: a narrowband license; paired three-megahertz channels (3/3 broadband licenses); and paired five-megahertz channels (5/5 licenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing regime: prospective licensees should select among defined license types and comply with associated technical rules and application processes for each license option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegations for settling FTCA and MPCECA claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission modifies rules regarding the delegated authority of the Chairman and the Managing Director to settle claims filed against the agency under the Federal Tort Claims Act and the Military Personnel and Civilian Employees' Claims Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal agency authority: changes specify limits and procedures for settlement authority; affects how claim settlements against the Commission are processed and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlicensed geofenced variable power (GVP) device operational limits
rubrics_metrics.description: GVP devices operating in the U-NII-5 and U-NII-7 portions of the 6 GHz band (5.925-7.125 GHz) may operate at up to 11 dBm/MHz EIRP power spectral density and 24 dBm EIRP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical limits: GVP devices are permitted higher power than very low power 6 GHz devices but must comply with power spectral density and EIRP caps; manufacturers and operators must ensure devices meet these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geofencing and exclusion zones for GVP devices
rubrics_metrics.description: GVP devices must use geofencing systems to prevent harmful interference to licensed microwave links and radio astronomy observatories; geofencing systems will calculate exclusion zones where GVP devices cannot operate on specified frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation requirements: each GVP access point must have geolocation capability to determine location and avoid operating on prohibited frequencies within exclusion zones; device/management systems must integrate geofencing to enforce exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client device power relative to access point (6 dB rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Client devices must operate 6 dB below the access point's authorized power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device behavior requirement: client devices must be configured/limited to operate at the specified power differential to reduce interference risks; compliance testing and certification should reflect this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of WRC-15 implementations and related corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission issues final rules implementing WRC-15 decisions and makes corrections where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative: corrections may be issued to previously published final rules to fix errors; stakeholders should consult corrected final rules for authoritative text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering access controls for VoIP providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt rules regarding direct access to numbers by providers of interconnected VoIP services to reduce access to telephone numbers by potential perpetrators of illegal robocalls consistent with Congressional directives (e.g., TRACED Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and safeguards: rules aim to safeguard numbering resources and consumers, protect national security, promote public safety, and ensure compliance with other Commission rules; providers seeking direct access must meet specified requirements and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: TV channel substitution and principal community coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituting a TV channel (e.g., *33 for *8 at Hutchinson, Kansas) is acceptable where staff engineering analysis finds the proposal complies with the Commission's principal community coverage and technical requirements and is not predicted to result in viewer loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering/coverage test: substitutions must maintain or improve principal community coverage and comply with technical rules; applicants should provide engineering analyses demonstrating compliance and lack of viewer loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacant FM channel compliance with city-grade and separation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Vacant FM channels that are not in compliance with minimum distance separation or city-grade coverage requirements must be remedied before applications may be opened; substitution may be used to bring channels into compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural: the Commission may amend the Table of FM Allotments to substitute compliant channels and delay opening filing windows until compliance is achieved/addressed in subsequent orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB approval of information collections before effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a rule change involves information collection requirements, OMB approval under the Paperwork Reduction Act must be obtained and announced (e.g., Robocall Mitigation Database amendments) before the amended provisions become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing/implementation: Commission will publish documents announcing effective dates after OMB approval; regulated entities should not rely on amended obligations until officially announced effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of rule deletions when significant adverse comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct final repeal instructions for identified obsolete rules may be withdrawn if they draw 'significant adverse' public comments or if the Commission determines additional notice-and-comment procedures are required; withdrawn repeals result in retention of the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process: when adverse comments are received, the Commission may convert a direct final rule action into a proceeding requiring further notice and comment and retain the affected rule parts pending that process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and technical updates for low power and Class A TV services
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission adopts operational and technical rule updates for Class A television, low power television, and TV translator stations to provide clarity and regulatory certainty for licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory clarity: updates address operations and technical parameters and are intended to help licensees make informed business decisions; licensees should review the adopted changes for compliance and opportunities to improve service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection approvals and administrative corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission announces OMB approvals for information collections associated with adopted rules (e.g., hearing aid compatibility, robocall database amendments) and may correct typographical/formatting errors in final rules published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance and recordkeeping: stakeholders should note OMB control numbers and watch for corrections to final rules that may affect compliance obligations; administrative corrections do not change substantive obligations but fix errors in published text.
